# Evaluation & Guardrails {.topic-h1}

How to know whether a model or an agent is good enough, and how to stop a bad answer before it reaches anyone: measuring quality on test sets, and enforcing rules on every request.
:::

::: {.compare}
::: {.col}
**Evaluation: measure**

*Is my model or agent good enough?* Run it on a **test set**, before release and continuously, and get **scores**: accuracy, success rate, regressions between versions.

*"On 200 questions, v2 answers correctly 87% of the time, v1 81%."*
:::
::: {.col}
**Guardrails: prevent**

*How do I stop **this** answer from causing harm?* Check **every request**, in real time, and take an **action**: block, rewrite, retry, or call a human.

*"This message contains a prompt injection attempt: refused."*
:::
:::

The two use the same tools in opposite directions. A guardrail is often an evaluator running live, like an LLM-as-a-judge that scores each answer before it is shown. And guardrails are themselves evaluated: choosing a threshold means counting false positives (good answers blocked) and false negatives (bad answers let through).
